title: Final Capstone: Your Own Project
description: The last project is yours to choose: build something you care about, properly, with everything the course has taught.
hints: Keep it small enough to finish in a few weeks. A finished small program teaches more than a big unfinished one, and the first version can leave out half the ideas.
Build it in thin slices: something that runs end to end on day one, however crude, then one feature at a time with a commit (or a saved copy) after each.

If you get stuck on how to structure it, go back to the projects you have done: the to-do list (milestone 5), the library (6), the battle arena (8) and the key-value database (10) are each a pattern you can reuse.
requirements: Pick something you care about. Ideas: a small game, a ray tracer that writes PPM images, a text editor, a CHIP-8 emulator, an interpreter for a tiny language
Write a short design note first: what it does, the main classes, how data flows
Use what the course taught on purpose: RAII and no raw `new`/`delete`, the right containers, classes with clear invariants, error handling with exceptions or `std::expected`
Tests for its core logic (your own test framework from project 4 is fine)
Measure one slow part and make it faster, with the before and after times in a comment
stretch: Move it to a real repository on your own machine with CMake, sanitizer builds and continuous integration (lessons 10.09 and 13.09).
